<from node="igors-macbook-pro"/> Lets implement the user <> role <> permission relation in the db. with short lived (under 5min, be sure invalidate on changes) backend side cache.

Make the superuser functionality to be in the roles as well with permission “super”.
Here is additional information from the task:
# Ender Turing Full-Stack Developer Test Task

This assignment is for a developer role at Ender Turing.

Add role-aware access control to the existing
[Full-Stack FastAPI Template](https://github.com/fastapi/full-stack-fastapi-template/tree/master).

The stack is FastAPI, SQLModel, PostgreSQL, React and TypeScript.

## Timebox

Aim for about **one hour**. Submit the best coherent solution you can within that
time and state how long you actually spent.

AI coding tools are allowed. You remain responsible for every submitted change.

Prioritize working, understandable code. There is no bonus for extensive
documentation, diagrams, agent configuration, generated reports or a large number
of tests.

## Product requirements

Introduce three access levels:

- **Admin** can manage users and their access.
- **Manager** can view users and metrics, but cannot change user access.
- **Member** can access and update their own profile.

The metrics page may be a simple stub. Existing application features should keep
working unless a change is necessary for the new access model.

Authorization must be enforced by the backend. The frontend should reflect the
same access rules and handle direct navigation to unauthorized pages sensibly.

For behavior that is not specified, make reasonable assumptions and implement
them consistently.

## Existing production context

Treat the template as an already deployed application, not a new project:

- The database contains existing users created with the current `is_superuser`
  model.
- Existing data must survive the migration without unintended privilege changes.
- Access or active-status changes must affect users who already have a session.
- Assume migrations run against a populated database.

You decide how roles or permissions are represented, how compatibility is handled,
where authorization checks live, and how the backend and frontend communicate
access information.

## Expected implementation

- A database migration for any schema changes.
- Backend and frontend behavior for all three access levels.
- Focused automated tests for the security-critical behavior you consider most
  important.
- A minimal way for the reviewer to exercise all three access levels locally.
- Existing project setup and test commands should continue to work. If your changes
  require different commands, update the relevant instructions.

Keep the change focused. Unrelated refactoring, infrastructure work and visual
polish are outside the task.

## Submission

Provide only:

1. A GitHub repository or pull request containing the working implementation and
   its commit history.
2. The commands needed to run the solution and its tests, if they differ from the
   original template.
3. The **complete raw export** of every AI coding conversation used for the task,
   committed under `ai-conversations/`.

The AI export must contain the original prompts and responses. A summary,
retelling, selected excerpts or generated description of the conversation is not
a replacement for the raw export. Remove secrets if necessary and mark any
redactions clearly.

The code is the primary deliverable. We will review correctness, security,
maintainability, consistency, migration safety, scope control, and how the AI tool
was directed and validated.

Be prepared to explain the implementation and make a small change to an access
rule during a follow-up conversation.

import uuid
from datetime import UTC, datetime

from pydantic import EmailStr
from sqlmodel import Field, Relationship, SQLModel


def get_datetime_utc() -> datetime:
    return datetime.now(UTC)


# Shared properties
class UserBase(SQLModel):
    email: EmailStr = Field(unique=True, index=True, max_length=255)
    is_active: bool = True
    is_superuser: bool = False
    full_name: str | None = Field(default=None, max_length=255)


# Properties to receive via API on creation
class UserCreate(UserBase):
    password: str = Field(min_length=8, max_length=128)


class UserRegister(SQLModel):
    email: EmailStr = Field(max_length=255)
    password: str = Field(min_length=8, max_length=128)
    full_name: str | None = Field(default=None, max_length=255)


# Properties to receive via API on update, all are optional
class UserUpdate(SQLModel):
    email: EmailStr | None = Field(default=None, max_length=255)
    is_active: bool | None = None
    is_superuser: bool | None = None
    full_name: str | None = Field(default=None, max_length=255)
    password: str | None = Field(default=None, min_length=8, max_length=128)


class UserUpdateMe(SQLModel):
    full_name: str | None = Field(default=None, max_length=255)
    email: EmailStr | None = Field(default=None, max_length=255)


class UpdatePassword(SQLModel):
    current_password: str = Field(min_length=8, max_length=128)
    new_password: str = Field(min_length=8, max_length=128)


# Database model, database table inferred from class name
class User(UserBase, table=True):
    id: uuid.UUID = Field(default_factory=uuid.uuid4, primary_key=True)
    hashed_password: str
    created_at: datetime | None = Field(default_factory=get_datetime_utc)
    items: list[Item] = Relationship(back_populates="owner", cascade_delete=True)


# Properties to return via API, id is always required
class UserPublic(UserBase):
    id: uuid.UUID
    created_at: datetime | None = None


class UsersPublic(SQLModel):
    data: list[UserPublic]
    count: int


# Shared properties
class ItemBase(SQLModel):
    title: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=255)
    description: str | None = Field(default=None, max_length=255)


# Properties to receive on item creation
class ItemCreate(ItemBase):
    pass


# Properties to receive on item update
class ItemUpdate(SQLModel):
    title: str | None = Field(default=None, min_length=1, max_length=255)
    description: str | None = Field(default=None, max_length=255)


# Database model, database table inferred from class name
class Item(ItemBase, table=True):
    id: uuid.UUID = Field(default_factory=uuid.uuid4, primary_key=True)
    created_at: datetime | None = Field(default_factory=get_datetime_utc)
    owner_id: uuid.UUID = Field(
        foreign_key="user.id", nullable=False, ondelete="CASCADE"
    )
    owner: User | None = Relationship(back_populates="items")


# Properties to return via API, id is always required
class ItemPublic(ItemBase):
    id: uuid.UUID
    owner_id: uuid.UUID
    created_at: datetime | None = None


class ItemsPublic(SQLModel):
    data: list[ItemPublic]
    count: int


# Generic message
class Message(SQLModel):
    message: str


# JSON payload containing access token
class Token(SQLModel):
    access_token: str
    token_type: str = "bearer"


# Contents of JWT token
class TokenPayload(SQLModel):
    sub: str | None = None


class NewPassword(SQLModel):
    token: str
    new_password: str = Field(min_length=8, max_length=128)

from collections.abc import Generator
from typing import Annotated

import jwt
from fastapi import Depends, HTTPException, status
from fastapi.security import OAuth2PasswordBearer
from jwt.exceptions import InvalidTokenError
from pydantic import ValidationError
from sqlmodel import Session

from app.core import security
from app.core.config import settings
from app.core.db import engine
from app.models import TokenPayload, User

reusable_oauth2 = OAuth2PasswordBearer(
    tokenUrl=f"{settings.API_V1_STR}/login/access-token"
)


def get_db() -> Generator[Session]:
    with Session(engine) as session:
        yield session


SessionDep = Annotated[Session, Depends(get_db)]
TokenDep = Annotated[str, Depends(reusable_oauth2)]


def get_current_user(session: SessionDep, token: TokenDep) -> User:
    try:
        payload = jwt.decode(
            token, settings.SECRET_KEY, algorithms=[security.ALGORITHM]
        )
        token_data = TokenPayload(**payload)
    except InvalidTokenError, ValidationError:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=status.HTTP_403_FORBIDDEN,
            detail="Could not validate credentials",
        )
    user = session.get(User, token_data.sub)
    if not user:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="User not found")
    if not user.is_active:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="Inactive user")
    return user


CurrentUser = Annotated[User, Depends(get_current_user)]


def get_current_active_superuser(current_user: CurrentUser) -> User:
    if not current_user.is_superuser:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=403, detail="The user doesn't have enough privileges"
        )
    return current_user

import uuid
from typing import Any

from sqlmodel import Session, select

from app.core.security import get_password_hash, verify_password
from app.models import Item, ItemCreate, User, UserCreate, UserUpdate


def create_user(*, session: Session, user_create: UserCreate) -> User:
    db_obj = User.model_validate(
        user_create, update={"hashed_password": get_password_hash(user_create.password)}
    )
    session.add(db_obj)
    session.commit()
    session.refresh(db_obj)
    return db_obj


def update_user(*, session: Session, db_user: User, user_in: UserUpdate) -> Any:
    user_data = user_in.model_dump(exclude_unset=True)
    extra_data = {}
    if "password" in user_data:
        password = user_data["password"]
        hashed_password = get_password_hash(password)
        extra_data["hashed_password"] = hashed_password
    db_user.sqlmodel_update(user_data, update=extra_data)
    session.add(db_user)
    session.commit()
    session.refresh(db_user)
    return db_user


def get_user_by_email(*, session: Session, email: str) -> User | None:
    statement = select(User).where(User.email == email)
    session_user = session.exec(statement).first()
    return session_user


# Dummy hash to use for timing attack prevention when user is not found
# This is an Argon2 hash of a random password, used to ensure constant-time comparison
DUMMY_HASH = "$argon2id$v=19$m=65536,t=3,p=4$MjQyZWE1MzBjYjJlZTI0Yw$YTU4NGM5ZTZmYjE2NzZlZjY0ZWY3ZGRkY2U2OWFjNjk"


def authenticate(*, session: Session, email: str, password: str) -> User | None:
    db_user = get_user_by_email(session=session, email=email)
    if not db_user:
        # Prevent timing attacks by running password verification even when user doesn't exist
        # This ensures the response time is similar whether or not the email exists
        verify_password(password, DUMMY_HASH)
        return None
    verified, updated_password_hash = verify_password(password, db_user.hashed_password)
    if not verified:
        return None
    if updated_password_hash:
        db_user.hashed_password = updated_password_hash
        session.add(db_user)
        session.commit()
        session.refresh(db_user)
    return db_user


def create_item(*, session: Session, item_in: ItemCreate, owner_id: uuid.UUID) -> Item:
    db_item = Item.model_validate(item_in, update={"owner_id": owner_id})
    session.add(db_item)
    session.commit()
    session.refresh(db_item)
    return db_item

import warnings
from typing import Literal, Self

from pydantic import (
    EmailStr,
    HttpUrl,
    PostgresDsn,
    computed_field,
    field_validator,
    model_validator,
)
from pydantic_settings import BaseSettings, SettingsConfigDict


class Settings(BaseSettings):
    model_config = SettingsConfigDict(
        # Use top level .env file (one level above ./backend/)
        env_file="../.env",
        env_ignore_empty=True,
        extra="ignore",
    )
    API_V1_STR: str = "/api/v1"
    SECRET_KEY: str
    # 60 minutes * 24 hours * 8 days = 8 days
    ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES: int = 60 * 24 * 8
    FRONTEND_HOST: str = "http://localhost:5173"
    FASTAPI_ENV: Literal["development"] | None = None

    PROJECT_NAME: str
    SENTRY_DSN: HttpUrl | None = None
    DATABASE_URL: PostgresDsn

    @field_validator("DATABASE_URL", mode="before")
    @classmethod
    def _use_psycopg_driver(cls, value: str | PostgresDsn) -> str:
        database_url = str(value)
        for scheme in ("postgres://", "postgresql://"):
            if database_url.startswith(scheme):
                return database_url.replace(scheme, "postgresql+psycopg://", 1)
        return database_url

    SMTP_TLS: bool = True
    SMTP_SSL: bool = False
    SMTP_PORT: int = 587
    SMTP_HOST: str | None = None
    SMTP_USER: str | None = None
    SMTP_PASSWORD: str | None = None
    EMAILS_FROM_EMAIL: EmailStr | None = None
    EMAILS_FROM_NAME: str | None = None

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _set_default_emails_from(self) -> Self:
        if not self.EMAILS_FROM_NAME:
            self.EMAILS_FROM_NAME = self.PROJECT_NAME
        return self

    EMAIL_RESET_TOKEN_EXPIRE_HOURS: int = 48

    @computed_field  # type: ignore[prop-decorator]
    @property
    def emails_enabled(self) -> bool:
        return bool(self.SMTP_HOST and self.EMAILS_FROM_EMAIL)

    EMAIL_TEST_USER: EmailStr = "test@example.com"
    FIRST_SUPERUSER: EmailStr
    FIRST_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD: str

    def _check_default_secret(self, var_name: str, value: str | None) -> None:
        if value == "changethis":
            message = (
                f'The value of {var_name} is "changethis", '
                "for security, please change it, at least for deployments."
            )
            if self.FASTAPI_ENV == "development":
                warnings.warn(message, stacklevel=1)
            else:
                raise ValueError(message)

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _enforce_non_default_secrets(self) -> Self:
        self._check_default_secret("SECRET_KEY", self.SECRET_KEY)
        for host in self.DATABASE_URL.hosts():
            self._check_default_secret("DATABASE_URL password", host["password"])
        self._check_default_secret(
            "FIRST_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD", self.FIRST_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD
        )

        return self


settings = Settings()  # type: ignore # ty: ignore[unused-ignore-comment]

from datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta
from typing import Any

import jwt
from pwdlib import PasswordHash
from pwdlib.hashers.argon2 import Argon2Hasher
from pwdlib.hashers.bcrypt import BcryptHasher

from app.core.config import settings

password_hash = PasswordHash(
    (
        Argon2Hasher(),
        BcryptHasher(),
    )
)


ALGORITHM = "HS256"


def create_access_token(subject: str | Any, expires_delta: timedelta) -> str:
    expire = datetime.now(UTC) + expires_delta
    to_encode = {"exp": expire, "sub": str(subject)}
    encoded_jwt = jwt.encode(to_encode, settings.SECRET_KEY, algorithm=ALGORITHM)
    return encoded_jwt


def verify_password(
    plain_password: str, hashed_password: str
) -> tuple[bool, str | None]:
    return password_hash.verify_and_update(plain_password, hashed_password)


def get_password_hash(password: str) -> str:
    return password_hash.hash(password)

Agent definition commands

Usage: adi-mono agents [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  list          List agent definitions
  show          Show one agent definition
  save          Create or replace an agent definition
  run           Launch an agent in its backend. Pty executors open an interactive session and process executors run a headless CLI in the background
  awaits        The wakes a conversation is holding: what it is waiting on, and what to do about it
  runs          List runs across every agent (or one), newest first, with what became of each
  limit         Show, or set, how many agent runs may be live at once — overall, or (with `--project`) for one project's agents. The caps bind every launch the platform makes on its own (a trigger firing, a queued chat turn); a human overrides them per run with `agents run --force`
  spawn-policy  Show, or set, whether an `agent:<name>` launch outside the caller's own `can_spawn` is actually refused (ADI-MONO-113). `observe` (the default) never refuses one — it only logs it and publishes `adi.agents.spawn.refused` — until an operator has seen what switching to `enforce` would change and does so on purpose
  questions     List the questions runs are waiting on a person to answer
  answer        Answer the question a conversation is waiting on, and let it carry on
  stop          Stop a running agent using its executor's lifecycle
  rm            Delete an agent definition
  delete        Delete an agent definition
  migrate       Bring every agent definition up to the shape this binary writes, and record on each file that it happened
  help          Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --flavor <ID>
          Which install to act on: `release` (the default), `dev`, or any other flavour id.
          
          Equivalent to `ADI_FLAVOR`, and composes with the per-field `ADI_*` overrides the same way. Without it every command addresses the real install — which is the right default, and the reason it is spelled out rather than inferred from anything.

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

===== agents run help =====
Launch an agent in its backend. Pty executors open an interactive session and process executors run a headless CLI in the background

Usage: adi-mono agents run [OPTIONS] <NAME> [TASK]

Arguments:
  <NAME>
          

  [TASK]
          The task sent to a process backend, e.g. `adi-mono agents run my-agent "do the thing"`. Ignored by pty backends — an interactive session takes no task, it's typed into once the session opens. Same as `-m`/`--message`; giving both is refused. Leave it off entirely and a process backend is sent the placeholder task "run" (with a one-line notice on stderr), since forgetting it is far more likely than meaning it

Options:
      --flavor <ID>
          Which install to act on: `release` (the default), `dev`, or any other flavour id.
          
          Equivalent to `ADI_FLAVOR`, and composes with the per-field `ADI_*` overrides the same way. Without it every command addresses the real install — which is the right default, and the reason it is spelled out rather than inferred from anything.

  -m, --message <TASK>
          Same as the positional TASK, for a caller that already writes `-m`

      --pre-run <COMMAND>
          A command to really run before this run's first message reaches the model, after the agent's own `--prelude`. Repeatable, run in order; its real output is carried into the opening message, labelled as the tool call it was.
          
          For a launcher that already knows the agent's first move: filing a task and launching the agent to work it means you hold the id, so `--pre-run "adi-mono tasks show <id>"` hands over the task instead of writing an instruction the agent spends a turn obeying.

      --dir <PATH>
          Where this run starts, overriding the agent's own `working_dir` and its project directory. For pointing one agent at a different target each run

      --set <KEY=VALUE>
          A setting this run replaces in the agent's definition — `--set model=opus`, `--set permission_mode=bypassPermissions`, `--set unattended=true`. Repeatable.
          
          For the launch that is deliberately unlike the others, without editing the agent and having to edit it back. `--set <key>=` (nothing after the `=`) *unsets* the agent's own value for this run, back to the engine's default. The conversation keeps whatever is set here for every later turn, so a chat cannot answer its second message as a different agent than its first.

      --force
          Launch even when as many runs are already live as the store allows. The deliberate override of the concurrency limit — for a human who wants this one now

      --no-await
          Don't register the wake that would report this run back to whoever launched it.
          
          Only means anything when an agent is the one launching: a run that starts another agent is woken when it ends (see `agents awaits`), and this is how it says up front that it does not want to be. From a terminal there is nobody to wake and nothing is registered either way.

      --wait
          Block until the run finishes, print its answer, and exit with its status.
          
          What turns a launch into something another program can be composed out of: a shell script, a CI step, or an agent's own `Bash` — which is how one agent waits for another without either of them learning a new verb. Not for interactive backends: a pty run has no ending to wait for, only a pane somebody is looking at.

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

Add role-aware access control (RBAC) to the Full-Stack FastAPI template. Implement a
user <-> role <-> permission relation in the DB, enforce authorization in the backend,
reflect the same rules in the frontend, add a short-lived (<5min) server-side permission
cache that is invalidated on changes, and migrate the existing `is_superuser` model into a
role with permission "super". Three access levels: Admin, Manager, Member.

LOCKED ARCHITECTURE (contract — all specialists build to this)

Permissions (atomic string names):
  - super        : unrestricted; a holder passes EVERY permission check (back-compat for old superuser)
  - users:read   : list/view any user; view roles list
  - users:manage : create/update/delete users AND change their role assignments ("manage access")
  - metrics:read : view metrics page/endpoint

Roles (seeded, by name):
  - admin   -> {super, users:read, users:manage, metrics:read}
  - manager -> {users:read, metrics:read}
  - member  -> {}   (baseline self-service only: own profile, own password, own items — no special perm)

DB schema (SQLModel, new tables):
  - Permission(id uuid pk, name str unique index, description str|None)
  - Role(id uuid pk, name str unique index, description str|None)
  - RolePermission(role_id fk->role pk, permission_id fk->permission pk)   # M2M
  - UserRole(user_id fk->user pk, role_id fk->role pk)                     # M2M
  - User: DROP the stored `is_superuser` column; add roles: list[Role] via UserRole.

is_superuser compatibility (critical for migration safety + existing tests):
  - UserCreate.is_superuser (default False) stays accepted as INPUT; True => assign admin role on create.
    UserUpdate.is_superuser (optional) stays accepted; True => add admin role, False => remove super-bearing role(s).
    (This keeps init_db(..., is_superuser=True), routes/private.py, and existing tests working.)
  - Add role_ids: list[uuid] | None to UserCreate/UserUpdate for explicit role assignment (admin-only path).
  - UserPublic exposes is_superuser as a COMPUTED field = ("super" in resolved permissions),
    plus new fields roles: list[str] (role names) and permissions: list[str] (resolved perm names).
  - Self-protection "superusers can't delete themselves" => "users with `super` permission can't delete themselves."

Authorization layer (backend/app/api/deps.py):
  - get_current_user unchanged (loads fresh user each request, 400 if inactive) — this already makes
    active-status changes affect existing sessions.
  - resolve_permissions(session, user) -> set[str], served through the cache (below).
  - require_permission(perm) dependency factory: 403 unless perm in resolved perms OR "super" present.
  - Keep get_current_active_superuser == require_permission("super") for back-compat.

Route authorization changes (backend/app/api/routes/users.py etc.):
  - GET  /users/            -> users:read     (admin+manager; member 403; anon 401)
  - POST /users/            -> users:manage   (admin only)
  - PATCH /users/{id}       -> users:manage   (admin only; accepts role_ids)
  - DELETE /users/{id}      -> users:manage   (admin only)
  - GET  /users/{id}        -> self always OK; otherwise users:read
  - POST /utils/test-email  -> keep super (admin only)
  - password-recovery-html-content -> keep super
  - NEW GET /roles/         -> users:read (role selector for admin UI)
  - NEW GET /metrics/ (own router) -> metrics:read (admin+manager). Simple stub: counts (total users,
    active users, users per role). Member 403, anon 401.
  - /users/me, /users/me/password, DELETE /users/me, items/* ownership -> unchanged (member self-service).
  - PATCH /users/me must NOT allow changing roles/permissions/is_superuser (UserUpdateMe has no such fields) — assert this.

Short-lived permission cache (new module, e.g. backend/app/core/permissions.py):
  - In-process TTL cache: user_id -> (frozenset[str] perms, expires_at). TTL default 60s
    (settings.PERMISSIONS_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS, well under the 5-min requirement). threading.Lock guarded.
  - invalidate_user(user_id) on: user update, role assignment change, deactivation, deletion.
  - invalidate_all() available for role->permission changes.
  - Document the single-process limitation (multi-worker would need Redis) — do NOT implement Redis (scope).

Session/access invalidation requirements (must be true & tested):
  - Deactivating a user -> their existing JWT yields 400 on next request.
  - Demoting a manager to member -> next GET /users/ is 403 (cache invalidated on change, not after TTL).
  - Promoting a member to manager -> next GET /users/ is 200.

  - upgrade(): create permission/role/rolepermission/userrole tables; data-migrate seed the 3 roles,
    4 permissions, and their links; backfill userrole from existing users.is_superuser
    (True->admin, False->member); then DROP users.is_superuser.
  - downgrade(): add is_superuser column back, backfill True for users with admin/super role, drop link tables + role + permission.
  - Must be safe against a populated DB.

Reviewer local exercise:
  - Seed demo users in development only (idempotent, dev-gated): manager@example.com and member@example.com
    with password "changethis" alongside the existing admin@example.com. Document the three logins.

Tests (security-critical focus) — see child task for the checklist. Existing suite (58 tests) MUST stay green.

SEQUENCING
  1. fsf-backend: tests-first (author RBAC checklist) -> model -> migration -> cache -> enforcement -> green.
  2. fsf-frontend: once backend OpenAPI is stable, regenerate client + reflect rules + guard routes + role UI + metrics stub.
  3. fsf-secops: security review of the whole change.

Baseline: existing backend suite is GREEN (58 passed) as of start. FASTAPI_ENV=development, DB at :8071.
"""

out = sh(['adi-mono', 'tasks', 'add', 'RBAC: user<->role<->permission access control (Admin/Manager/Member)',
          '--project', 'full-stack-fastapi', '--cwd', ROOT, '--details', parent_details.strip(), '--json'])
print(out)

Everything is set up and **fsf-backend is now working test-first**. I'll be woken when it sends its interim checklist report (or finishes/asks). Here's where things stand and the plan I locked in — tell me if any access rule should differ.

## What I've done
- **Confirmed the safety net**: existing backend suite is green — **58 passed** — before any change. (The suite wipes dev-DB users on teardown; I re-seeded `admin@example.com`.)
- Created the task tree under **`FULL-STACK-FASTAPI-1`** (parent holds the full locked architecture):
  - **-2** backend, tests-first → launched on **fsf-backend** now
  - **-3** frontend → fsf-frontend (waits for a stable API contract)
  - **-4** security review → fsf-secops (waits for both)

## Access model (the three levels)
Authorization is enforced in the **backend**; the frontend mirrors it. Old `is_superuser` becomes the **`super`** permission carried by the **admin** role.

| Capability | permission | Admin | Manager | Member |
|---|---|:--:|:--:|:--:|
| Full/unrestricted | `super` | ✅ | — | — |
| List/view any user | `users:read` | ✅ | ✅ | — |
| Create/update/delete users **& change their access** | `users:manage` | ✅ | — | — |
| View metrics | `metrics:read` | ✅ | ✅ | — |
| Own profile / password / own items | (baseline) | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |

## The strict checklist (tests fsf-backend writes first)
1. Seed integrity: `admin`/`manager`/`member` exist with exactly the permission sets above
2. `/users/me` returns `roles` + `permissions` + computed `is_superuser`
3. `GET /users/` → admin 200 · manager 200 · member 403 · anon 401
4. `POST /users/` → admin ✅ · manager 403 · member 403
5. `PATCH /users/{id}` → admin ✅ · manager 403 · member 403
6. `DELETE /users/{id}` → admin ✅ · manager 403 · member 403
7. `GET /users/{id}` → self 200 for all; other-user → admin/manager 200 · member 403
8. Role assignment (`users:manage`) → admin ✅ · manager 403; manager **cannot** escalate self
9. `GET /metrics/` → admin 200 · manager 200 · member 403 · anon 401
10. Member self-service preserved (profile, password, own items)
11. `PATCH /users/me` cannot change role/permission/`is_superuser`
12. **Session/access invalidation** (most security-critical): deactivation → next request 400; demote manager→member → next `GET /users/` 403 immediately; promote member→manager → 200
13. `is_superuser` back-compat: created with `is_superuser=True` ⇒ super perm + admin role
14. Cache unit test: resolves, `invalidate_user` forces fresh resolve, TTL < 300s

## Key design decisions (redirect me if you'd prefer otherwise)
- **Many-to-many** user↔role↔permission (true RBAC), seeded one role per user.
- **Drop the stored `is_superuser` column**; keep it as a *computed* API field (`"super" in permissions`) and still *accept* it as input mapped to the admin role — so `init_db`, the private route, and all existing tests keep working, and the migration backfills roles from the old column (superuser→admin, others→member) with no privilege change.
- **Cache**: in-process TTL (default **60s**, ≪5min), invalidated on every role/active-status/user change so demotions and deactivations take effect immediately, not after TTL. Single-process only (documented; Redis is out of scope).
- Reviewer convenience: dev-only seed of `manager@example.com` + `member@example.com` (`changethis`) beside the existing admin.

I'll report back as soon as fsf-backend lands the red checklist.

import uuid
from datetime import UTC, datetime

from pydantic import EmailStr, model_validator
from sqlmodel import Field, Relationship, SQLModel


def get_datetime_utc() -> datetime:
    return datetime.now(UTC)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# RBAC link tables (many-to-many association tables)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
class UserRole(SQLModel, table=True):
    user_id: uuid.UUID = Field(
        foreign_key="user.id", primary_key=True, ondelete="CASCADE"
    )
    role_id: uuid.UUID = Field(
        foreign_key="role.id", primary_key=True, ondelete="CASCADE"
    )


class RolePermission(SQLModel, table=True):
    role_id: uuid.UUID = Field(
        foreign_key="role.id", primary_key=True, ondelete="CASCADE"
    )
    permission_id: uuid.UUID = Field(
        foreign_key="permission.id", primary_key=True, ondelete="CASCADE"
    )


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# RBAC core tables
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
class Permission(SQLModel, table=True):
    id: uuid.UUID = Field(default_factory=uuid.uuid4, primary_key=True)
    name: str = Field(unique=True, index=True, max_length=255)
    description: str | None = Field(default=None, max_length=255)
    roles: list[Role] = Relationship(
        back_populates="permissions", link_model=RolePermission
    )


class Role(SQLModel, table=True):
    id: uuid.UUID = Field(default_factory=uuid.uuid4, primary_key=True)
    name: str = Field(unique=True, index=True, max_length=255)
    description: str | None = Field(default=None, max_length=255)
    permissions: list[Permission] = Relationship(
        back_populates="roles", link_model=RolePermission
    )
    users: list[User] = Relationship(back_populates="roles", link_model=UserRole)


# Shared properties
class UserBase(SQLModel):
    email: EmailStr = Field(unique=True, index=True, max_length=255)
    is_active: bool = True
    full_name: str | None = Field(default=None, max_length=255)


# Properties to receive via API on creation
class UserCreate(UserBase):
    password: str = Field(min_length=8, max_length=128)
    # Back-compat input: True assigns the admin (super-bearing) role on create.
    is_superuser: bool = False
    # Explicit role assignment (admin-only path).
    role_ids: list[uuid.UUID] | None = None


class UserRegister(SQLModel):
    email: EmailStr = Field(max_length=255)
    password: str = Field(min_length=8, max_length=128)
    full_name: str | None = Field(default=None, max_length=255)


# Properties to receive via API on update, all are optional
class UserUpdate(SQLModel):
    email: EmailStr | None = Field(default=None, max_length=255)
    is_active: bool | None = None
    # Back-compat input: True adds admin role, False removes super-bearing role(s).
    is_superuser: bool | None = None
    full_name: str | None = Field(default=None, max_length=255)
    password: str | None = Field(default=None, min_length=8, max_length=128)
    # Explicit role assignment (admin-only path).
    role_ids: list[uuid.UUID] | None = None


class UserUpdateMe(SQLModel):
    full_name: str | None = Field(default=None, max_length=255)
    email: EmailStr | None = Field(default=None, max_length=255)


class UpdatePassword(SQLModel):
    current_password: str = Field(min_length=8, max_length=128)
    new_password: str = Field(min_length=8, max_length=128)


# Database model, database table inferred from class name
class User(UserBase, table=True):
    id: uuid.UUID = Field(default_factory=uuid.uuid4, primary_key=True)
    hashed_password: str
    created_at: datetime | None = Field(default_factory=get_datetime_utc)
    items: list[Item] = Relationship(back_populates="owner", cascade_delete=True)
    roles: list[Role] = Relationship(back_populates="users", link_model=UserRole)

    @property
    def permission_names(self) -> set[str]:
        """Resolve the union of permission names granted by this user's roles."""
        return {
            permission.name for role in self.roles for permission in role.permissions
        }

    @property
    def is_superuser(self) -> bool:
        """Back-compat flag: holds the unrestricted ``super`` permission."""
        return "super" in self.permission_names


# Properties to return via API, id is always required
class UserPublic(UserBase):
    id: uuid.UUID
    created_at: datetime | None = None
    # Computed from the resolved permission set.
    is_superuser: bool = False
    roles: list[str] = []
    permissions: list[str] = []

    @model_validator(mode="before")
    @classmethod
    def _resolve_from_user(cls, data: object) -> object:
        # When validating a ``User`` ORM instance, flatten its roles/permissions.
        if isinstance(data, User):
            perms = data.permission_names
            return {
                "id": data.id,
                "email": data.email,
                "is_active": data.is_active,
                "full_name": data.full_name,
                "created_at": data.created_at,
                "is_superuser": "super" in perms,
                "roles": sorted(role.name for role in data.roles),
                "permissions": sorted(perms),
            }
        return data

    data: list[UserPublic]
    count: int


# Role representation returned via API
class RolePublic(SQLModel):
    id: uuid.UUID
    name: str
    description: str | None = None
    permissions: list[str] = []

    @model_validator(mode="before")
    @classmethod
    def _resolve_from_role(cls, data: object) -> object:
        if isinstance(data, Role):
            return {
                "id": data.id,
                "name": data.name,
                "description": data.description,
                "permissions": sorted(p.name for p in data.permissions),
            }
        return data


class RolesPublic(SQLModel):
    data: list[RolePublic]
    count: int


# Metrics stub payload
class MetricsPublic(SQLModel):

    active_users: int
    users_per_role: dict[str, int]

class ItemBase(SQLModel):

    description: str | None = Field(default=None, max_length=255)

# Properties to receive on item update

# Database model, database table inferred from class name
class Item(ItemBase, table=True):
    id: uuid.UUID = Field(default_factory=uuid.uuid4, primary_key=True)
    created_at: datetime | None = Field(default_factory=get_datetime_utc)
    owner_id: uuid.UUID = Field(
        foreign_key="user.id", nullable=False, ondelete="CASCADE"
    )
    owner: User | None = Relationship(back_populates="items")


# Properties to return via API, id is always required
class ItemPublic(ItemBase):
    id: uuid.UUID
    owner_id: uuid.UUID
    created_at: datetime | None = None


class ItemsPublic(SQLModel):
    data: list[ItemPublic]
    count: int


# Generic message
class Message(SQLModel):
    message: str


# JSON payload containing access token
class Token(SQLModel):
    access_token: str
    token_type: str = "bearer"


# Contents of JWT token
class TokenPayload(SQLModel):
    sub: str | None = None


class NewPassword(SQLModel):

========================= core/permissions.py =========================
"""Short-lived, in-process permission cache.

Resolves the set of permission names granted to a user (via their roles) and
caches it for a short TTL so that repeated authorization checks within the same
request burst do not re-walk the role/permission relationships every time.

Invalidation is explicit: any change that can affect a user's effective
permissions (role assignment change, deactivation, deletion, update) calls
:func:`invalidate_user`; role->permission changes call :func:`invalidate_all`.

LIMITATION: the cache is per-process. Under a multi-worker / multi-process
deployment each worker keeps its own copy, so an invalidation in one worker is
not seen by the others; stale entries would still expire within the TTL. A
cross-process deployment would need a shared store (e.g. Redis) and a pub/sub
invalidation channel. That is intentionally out of scope here.
"""

import threading
import time
import uuid

from sqlmodel import Session, col, select

from app.core.config import settings
from app.models import Permission, RolePermission, User, UserRole

# user_id -> (frozenset of permission names, monotonic expiry timestamp)
_cache: dict[uuid.UUID, tuple[frozenset[str], float]] = {}
_lock = threading.Lock()


def _resolve_from_db(session: Session, user: User) -> frozenset[str]:
    """Resolve the user's permission names via user -> role -> permission joins."""
    statement = (
        select(Permission.name)
        .select_from(UserRole)
        .join(
            RolePermission,
            col(RolePermission.role_id) == col(UserRole.role_id),
        )
        .join(
            Permission,
            col(Permission.id) == col(RolePermission.permission_id),
        )
        .where(col(UserRole.user_id) == user.id)
        .distinct()
    )
    return frozenset(session.exec(statement).all())


def resolve_permissions(session: Session, user: User) -> set[str]:
    """Return the user's effective permission names, served through the cache."""
    now = time.monotonic()
    user_id = user.id
    with _lock:
        entry = _cache.get(user_id)
        if entry is not None and entry[1] > now:
            return set(entry[0])

    perms = _resolve_from_db(session, user)
    expires_at = time.monotonic() + settings.PERMISSIONS_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS
    with _lock:
        _cache[user_id] = (perms, expires_at)
    return set(perms)


def invalidate_user(user_id: uuid.UUID) -> None:
    """Drop one user's cached permission set (role change, deactivation, ...)."""
    with _lock:
        _cache.pop(user_id, None)


def invalidate_all() -> None:
    """Drop every cached entry (role->permission mapping changed)."""
    with _lock:
        _cache.clear()

from collections.abc import Callable, Generator
from typing import Annotated

import jwt
from fastapi import Depends, HTTPException, status
from fastapi.security import OAuth2PasswordBearer
from jwt.exceptions import InvalidTokenError
from pydantic import ValidationError
from sqlmodel import Session

from app.core import security
from app.core.config import settings
from app.core.db import engine
from app.core.permissions import resolve_permissions
from app.models import TokenPayload, User

reusable_oauth2 = OAuth2PasswordBearer(
    tokenUrl=f"{settings.API_V1_STR}/login/access-token"
)


def get_db() -> Generator[Session]:
    with Session(engine) as session:
        yield session


SessionDep = Annotated[Session, Depends(get_db)]
TokenDep = Annotated[str, Depends(reusable_oauth2)]


def get_current_user(session: SessionDep, token: TokenDep) -> User:
    try:
        payload = jwt.decode(
            token, settings.SECRET_KEY, algorithms=[security.ALGORITHM]
        )
        token_data = TokenPayload(**payload)
    except InvalidTokenError, ValidationError:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=status.HTTP_403_FORBIDDEN,
            detail="Could not validate credentials",
        )
    user = session.get(User, token_data.sub)
    if not user:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="User not found")
    if not user.is_active:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="Inactive user")
    return user


CurrentUser = Annotated[User, Depends(get_current_user)]


def get_current_permissions(session: SessionDep, current_user: CurrentUser) -> set[str]:
    """The effective permission names of the current user (cached)."""
    return resolve_permissions(session, current_user)


CurrentPermissions = Annotated[set[str], Depends(get_current_permissions)]


def require_permission(permission: str) -> Callable[..., User]:
    """Dependency factory: 403 unless the user holds ``permission`` or ``super``."""

    def dependency(current_user: CurrentUser, perms: CurrentPermissions) -> User:
        if "super" in perms or permission in perms:
            return current_user
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=403, detail="The user doesn't have enough privileges"
        )

    return dependency


def get_current_active_superuser(
    current_user: CurrentUser, perms: CurrentPermissions
) -> User:
    # Kept for back-compat: equivalent to require_permission("super").
    if "super" not in perms:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=403, detail="The user doesn't have enough privileges"
        )
    return current_user

========================= crud.py =========================
import uuid
from typing import Any

from sqlmodel import Session, select

from app.core.permissions import invalidate_user
from app.core.security import get_password_hash, verify_password
from app.models import (
    Item,
    ItemCreate,
    Role,
    User,
    UserCreate,
    UserUpdate,
)


def get_role_by_name(*, session: Session, name: str) -> Role | None:
    return session.exec(select(Role).where(Role.name == name)).first()


def _roles_from_ids(*, session: Session, role_ids: list[uuid.UUID]) -> list[Role]:
    roles: list[Role] = []
    for role_id in role_ids:
        role = session.get(Role, role_id)
        if role is not None and role not in roles:
            roles.append(role)
    return roles


def _resolve_create_roles(
    *, session: Session, is_superuser: bool, role_ids: list[uuid.UUID] | None
) -> list[Role]:
    """Decide which roles a newly created user receives.

    Precedence: explicit role_ids, plus the admin role when is_superuser is set.
    Falls back to the baseline ``member`` role so every user has at least the
    self-service level (mirrors the migration's is_superuser=False -> member).
    """
    roles: list[Role] = []
    if role_ids:
        roles = _roles_from_ids(session=session, role_ids=role_ids)
    if is_superuser:
        admin = get_role_by_name(session=session, name="admin")
        if admin is not None and admin not in roles:
            roles.append(admin)
    if not roles:
        member = get_role_by_name(session=session, name="member")
        if member is not None:
            roles = [member]
    return roles


def create_user(*, session: Session, user_create: UserCreate) -> User:
    db_obj = User.model_validate(
        user_create, update={"hashed_password": get_password_hash(user_create.password)}
    )
    db_obj.roles = _resolve_create_roles(
        session=session,
        is_superuser=user_create.is_superuser,
        role_ids=user_create.role_ids,
    )
    session.add(db_obj)
    session.commit()
    session.refresh(db_obj)
    invalidate_user(db_obj.id)
    return db_obj


def update_user(*, session: Session, db_user: User, user_in: UserUpdate) -> Any:
    user_data = user_in.model_dump(exclude_unset=True)
    extra_data = {}
    if "password" in user_data:
        password = user_data["password"]
        hashed_password = get_password_hash(password)
        extra_data["hashed_password"] = hashed_password

    # Role-related fields are not columns on User; apply them separately so
    # sqlmodel_update never tries to set the computed is_superuser property.
    role_ids = user_data.pop("role_ids", None)
    is_superuser = user_data.pop("is_superuser", None)

    db_user.sqlmodel_update(user_data, update=extra_data)

    if role_ids is not None:
        db_user.roles = _roles_from_ids(session=session, role_ids=role_ids)
    if is_superuser is not None:
        admin = get_role_by_name(session=session, name="admin")
        if is_superuser:
            if admin is not None and admin not in db_user.roles:
                db_user.roles.append(admin)
        else:
            # Drop any super-bearing role(s).
            db_user.roles = [
                role
                for role in db_user.roles
                if "super" not in {p.name for p in role.permissions}
            ]

    session.add(db_user)
    session.commit()
    session.refresh(db_user)
    invalidate_user(db_user.id)
    return db_user


def get_user_by_email(*, session: Session, email: str) -> User | None:
    statement = select(User).where(User.email == email)
    session_user = session.exec(statement).first()
    return session_user


# Dummy hash to use for timing attack prevention when user is not found
# This is an Argon2 hash of a random password, used to ensure constant-time comparison
DUMMY_HASH = "$argon2id$v=19$m=65536,t=3,p=4$MjQyZWE1MzBjYjJlZTI0Yw$YTU4NGM5ZTZmYjE2NzZlZjY0ZWY3ZGRkY2U2OWFjNjk"


def authenticate(*, session: Session, email: str, password: str) -> User | None:
    db_user = get_user_by_email(session=session, email=email)
    if not db_user:
        # Prevent timing attacks by running password verification even when user doesn't exist
        # This ensures the response time is similar whether or not the email exists
        verify_password(password, DUMMY_HASH)
        return None
    verified, updated_password_hash = verify_password(password, db_user.hashed_password)
    if not verified:
        return None
    if updated_password_hash:
        db_user.hashed_password = updated_password_hash
        session.add(db_user)
        session.commit()
        session.refresh(db_user)
    return db_user


def create_item(*, session: Session, item_in: ItemCreate, owner_id: uuid.UUID) -> Item:
    db_item = Item.model_validate(item_in, update={"owner_id": owner_id})
    session.add(db_item)
    session.commit()
    session.refresh(db_item)
    return db_item

from typing import Any

from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends
from sqlmodel import select

from app.api.deps import SessionDep, require_permission
from app.models import Role, RolePublic, RolesPublic

router = APIRouter(prefix="/roles", tags=["roles"])


@router.get(
    "/",
    dependencies=[Depends(require_permission("users:read"))],
    response_model=RolesPublic,
)
def read_roles(session: SessionDep) -> Any:
    """
    List roles (and their resolved permissions) for the admin role selector.
    """
    roles = session.exec(select(Role).order_by(Role.name)).all()
    data = [RolePublic.model_validate(role) for role in roles]
    return RolesPublic(data=data, count=len(data))

from typing import Any

from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends
from sqlmodel import col, func, select

from app.api.deps import SessionDep, require_permission
from app.models import MetricsPublic, Role, User

router = APIRouter(prefix="/metrics", tags=["metrics"])


@router.get(
    "/",
    dependencies=[Depends(require_permission("metrics:read"))],
    response_model=MetricsPublic,
)
def read_metrics(session: SessionDep) -> Any:
    """
    Simple metrics stub: total users, active users, and users per role.
    """
    total_users = session.exec(select(func.count()).select_from(User)).one()
    active_users = session.exec(
        select(func.count()).select_from(User).where(col(User.is_active).is_(True))
    ).one()
    roles = session.exec(select(Role)).all()
    users_per_role = {role.name: len(role.users) for role in roles}
    return MetricsPublic(
        total_users=total_users,
        active_users=active_users,
        users_per_role=users_per_role,
    )

Backend phase is **complete and independently verified** — I'll end my turn here to await the frontend. Summary of what I checked myself (not just trusting the sub-agent):

## Backend RBAC — done & verified ✅
**Tests:** `79 passed` (58 existing preserved + 21 new), lint clean. No existing test modified.

**Live behavior** against `http://full-stack-fastapi.adi`, all to contract:

| | roles | is_superuser | GET /users/ | /metrics/ | /roles/ | POST /users/ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| admin | `[admin]` | `true` | 200 | 200 | 200 | 200 |
| manager | `[manager]` | `false` | 200 | 200 | 200 | **403** |
| member | `[member]` | `false` | **403** | **403** | **403** | **403** |
| anon | — | — | **401** | **401** | — | — |

**Code I reviewed for correctness/consistency:**
- **Model** — `is_superuser` is now a computed property (`"super" in permissions`); M2M `User↔Role↔Permission`; `UserPublic` exposes `roles`/`permissions`; `role_ids` only on the admin-gated `UserUpdate`, **not** `UserUpdateMe` → no self-escalation path.
- **Cache** (`core/permissions.py`) — in-process TTL (60s ≪ 5min), lock-guarded, explicit join, `invalidate_user`/`invalidate_all`; invalidation wired into every create/update/delete. Single-process limitation documented.
- **Enforcement** (`deps.require_permission`) — `super`-or-specific; `get_current_user` still re-checks `is_active` each request, so deactivation + demotion take effect immediately (the invalidation tests prove it).
- **Migration** `3c2a211a9237` — creates tables, seeds, backfills `userrole` from `is_superuser` (super→admin, else→member) **before** dropping the column; downgrade re-adds it safely. Round-trip verified by fsf-backend.
- **Reviewer convenience** — dev-only demo logins `manager@example.com` / `member@example.com` (`changethis`) alongside `admin@example.com`.

**Housekeeping:** re-seeded the dev DB (test teardown wipes users), removed a stray `backend/server.log`, deleted a probe user I created during verification. Working tree holds only the intended RBAC changes (plus the pre-existing `.env` port edit). Nothing committed.

## In progress
- **fsf-frontend** (`FULL-STACK-FASTAPI-3`) is now regenerating the client and wiring the UI to the same rules (route guards, manager read-only Users, role selector, Metrics stub). I'll be woken when it lands, then run **fsf-secops** for the security review.

    )

# Security Review — RBAC implementation (FULL-STACK-FASTAPI-4)

## Verdict: ✅ SHIP — no blocking findings

The RBAC change is well-built and faithful to the LOCKED ARCHITECTURE. The backend is genuinely the authority, there is no privilege-escalation path, invalidation is immediate, the migration is safe, and the cache is correct. Everything below is informational/pre-existing; nothing blocks shipping.

I read every changed/new backend file, the migration, and the frontend guards, then **probed the live API with all three demo logins**, mutating and reverting state each time. **No code was changed; the working tree is identical to the start snapshot.**

## What I verified against each focus area

**(1) Backend is the authority** — confirmed live. Anon → 401, member → 403 on every protected route; the frontend guards are UX-only (redirect/hide) and the real enforcement is server-side.

| Endpoint | admin | manager | member | anon | Spec |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /users/` | 200 | 200 | 403 | 401 | users:read ✓ |
| `POST /users/` | — | 403 | 403 | 401 | users:manage ✓ |
| `PATCH/DELETE /users/{id}` | — | 403 | 403 | 401 | users:manage ✓ |
| `GET /roles/` | 200 | 200 | 403 | 401 | users:read ✓ |
| `GET /metrics/` | 200 | 200 | 403 | 401 | metrics:read ✓ |
| `POST /utils/test-email` | 201 | 403 | 403 | 401 | super ✓ |

**(2) Privilege escalation — none found.**
- `PATCH /users/me` (`users.py:85`) uses `UserUpdateMe` (only `full_name`/`email`); injected `is_superuser`/`role_ids`/`roles` are silently dropped by Pydantic (verified offline + live: member stayed `[]`).
- `POST /users/signup` → `UserRegister` drops `is_superuser`/`role_ids` before `UserCreate.model_validate` (verified: `is_superuser=False, role_ids=None`).
- Manager self-escalate via `PATCH /users/{self}` → **403** (needs `users:manage`, which manager lacks).
- `crud.update_user` (`crud.py:76`) pops `role_ids`/`is_superuser` before `sqlmodel_update`, so the computed `is_superuser` property is never mass-assigned.

**(3) Session/access invalidation — immediate, no TTL wait** (all verified live and reverted):
- Deactivate member → next request **400 "Inactive user"** (`deps.py:40`, fresh load each request).
- Demote manager→member → next `GET /users/` **403** (cache invalidated in `crud.update_user:102`).
- Promote member→manager → next `GET /users/` **200**.
- All mutation paths invalidate: `create_user`, `update_user`, route `delete_user`/`delete_user_me`; `seed_rbac` → `invalidate_all`.

**(4) Migration `3c2a211a9237`** — safe. Backfill: `is_superuser=true → admin`, else `member`; no unintended grants; `is_superuser` dropped last. Downgrade re-adds the column with `server_default false`, backfills `true` only for `super`-bearing roles, then drops default and tables in FK-safe order.

**(5) IDOR / self-delete** — `GET /users/{id}` (`users.py:166`): self always OK, otherwise `super`/`users:read` required (member→other = 403, member→nonexistent = 403, no existence oracle). Items enforce `owner_id == current_user.id`. Super-holder self-delete blocked on both `DELETE /users/me` and `DELETE /users/{id}`.

**(6) Cache** (`core/permissions.py`) — keyed by `user_id` (no cross-user poisoning), `threading.Lock`-guarded, TTL **60s < 5min**. Deployment runs a **single `fastapi run` worker**, so the in-process invalidation is reliable (the multi-worker limitation is documented and out of scope).

## Non-blocking findings

- **LOW (pre-existing, not RBAC)** — `backend/app/api/routes/private.py:24`: `POST /api/v1/private/users/` has **no auth** and is live on the dev host because `FASTAPI_ENV=development`. It builds `User()` directly (roleless, `is_superuser=False`), so **not an escalation vector**, but an open account-creation/enumeration surface. I confirmed it live and cleaned up the probe user. → filed **FULL-STACK-FASTAPI-5** for fsf-backend.
- **INFO** — `invalidate_all()` has no runtime caller (roles are immutable via API). Correct today; must be wired if a role-permission edit endpoint is ever added.
- **INFO (pre-existing)** — 8-day JWT lifetime (`config.py:25`) + token in `localStorage` (`useAuth.ts:45`); perms/active-status re-evaluated per request, but no revocation on password change.
- **INFO** — local `.env` keeps `changethis` secrets (dev warnings-only) and `DATABASE_URL` at `:8071` — the expected local setup; `config.py` raises on these outside dev.

One nice touch worth noting: `deps.py:37` uses `except InvalidTokenError, ValidationError:` — valid under Python 3.14 (PEP 758) and correctly catches both. Not a bug.

Adds a `user ↔ role ↔ permission` model to the template, enforced by the backend and mirrored in the frontend, with a short-lived server-side permission cache. The old `is_superuser` model is migrated into a role carrying a `super` permission.

### Access model
Authorization is enforced in the **backend**; the frontend mirrors it for UX. A holder of `super` passes every check.

| Capability | permission | Admin | Manager | Member |
|---|---|:--:|:--:|:--:|
| Unrestricted (old superuser) | `super` | ✅ | — | — |
| List/view any user, view roles | `users:read` | ✅ | ✅ | — |
| Create/update/delete users & change their access | `users:manage` | ✅ | — | — |
| View metrics | `metrics:read` | ✅ | ✅ | — |
| Own profile / password / own items | baseline | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |

### What's included
- **Schema + migration** (`3c2a211a9237`): `permission`, `role`, `rolepermission`, `userrole` tables (M2M); seeds `admin`/`manager`/`member` + 4 permissions; backfills `userrole` from the existing `is_superuser` (`True→admin`, else `member`) **before** dropping the column. Safe on a populated DB; reversible downgrade.
- **Compatibility**: `is_superuser` becomes a computed API field (`"super" in permissions`) and is still accepted as input (mapped to the admin role), so existing data, `init_db`, and the full original test suite are unchanged. `UserPublic` also exposes `roles[]` and `permissions[]`.

content.text:
Just the **resolved set of permission names for a user** — nothing else.

Concretely, in `backend/app/core/permissions.py` the cache is one module-level dict:

```python
# user_id -> (frozenset of permission names, expiry timestamp)
_cache: dict[uuid.UUID, tuple[frozenset[str], float]] = {}
```

- **Key**: the user's `id`.
- **Value**: the flattened union of permission names granted by *all* that user's roles — e.g. an admin caches `{"super", "users:read", "users:manage", "metrics:read"}`, a member caches `frozenset()`. Plus a monotonic expiry (**TTL 60s**, `settings.PERMISSIONS_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS`).

**Why**: resolving those names is a 3-table join (`userrole → rolepermission → permission`, in `_resolve_from_db`). Without the cache that join runs on every authorization check; with it, `require_permission()` reuses the set for up to 60s.

**What is deliberately *not* cached** (this is the security-relevant part):
- **Authentication** — every request still decodes the JWT and does `session.get(User)` fresh (`deps.py:get_current_user`).
- **`is_active`** — re-checked from the DB on every request, so a **deactivation takes effect immediately**, independent of the cache.
- **The displayed `roles[]`/`permissions[]`** in API responses — `UserPublic` computes those straight from the ORM object, so what the UI shows is always live.
- The user row, roles, or role→permission structure themselves — only the final flat name-set is kept.

**Invalidation**: `invalidate_user(user_id)` drops one entry on every user create/update/delete (so a role change or demotion reflects on the *next* request, not after the TTL); `invalidate_all()` clears everything when the role→permission seed changes. The 60s TTL is just a backstop. It's an in-process dict (one `fastapi` worker), guarded by a `threading.Lock`; the multi-process caveat is documented in the module.

Good question, and good instinct. Two things in your message — let me answer the gap question, then do the cache refactor you're describing.

**The 60s gap:** for a role *assignment* change made through the API (admin edits a user's `role_ids`), there's **no gap** — `crud.update_user` calls `invalidate_user(id)`, so the next request re-resolves. The 60s TTL only bites for changes that bypass the app: a direct DB edit, or a second worker in a multi-process deploy. The one real gap today is a *role-definition* change (editing which permissions a role grants) — there's no endpoint for that yet, and the current flat `user→perms` cache would need `invalidate_all()`. Your two-level design fixes exactly that. Let me look at the current cache test, then rebuild it.

Permissions are resolved in two cached layers that mirror the two relations,
rather than caching the flattened ``user -> permission`` set directly:

  * ``user -> role ids``    -- per user; small; changes only when that user's
    role assignment changes.
  * ``role -> permissions`` -- SHARED across every user that holds the role;
    changes only when a role's permission set is edited, which is rare.

A user's effective permissions are composed in memory by unioning the (cached)
permission sets of their (cached) roles. The expensive, rarely-changing
``role -> permission`` resolution is therefore cached ONCE and reused by every
user holding the role, instead of re-walking the full
``user -> role -> permission`` join and caching a separate flattened result per
user. With few roles and many users this is substantially less work and memory.

There is deliberately NO direct ``user -> permission`` relation: every
permission is granted through a role.

Invalidation is explicit and granular:
  * :func:`invalidate_user` -- a user's role assignment changed (or the user was
    deactivated / deleted / updated). Drops only that user's role-id entry.
  * :func:`invalidate_role` -- a role's permission set changed; every user that
    holds the role picks it up on their next request, via a single re-read of
    that one role (no need to touch any per-user entry).
  * :func:`invalidate_all` -- drop everything (e.g. after re-seeding).

LIMITATION: the cache is per-process. Under a multi-worker / multi-process
deployment each worker keeps its own copy, so an invalidation in one worker is
not seen by the others; stale entries would still expire within the TTL. A
cross-process deployment would need a shared store (e.g. Redis) and a pub/sub
invalidation channel. That is intentionally out of scope here.
"""

import threading
import time
import uuid

from sqlmodel import Session, col, select

from app.core.config import settings
from app.models import Permission, RolePermission, User, UserRole

# user_id -> (tuple of role ids, monotonic expiry)
_user_roles: dict[uuid.UUID, tuple[tuple[uuid.UUID, ...], float]] = {}
# role_id -> (frozenset of permission names, monotonic expiry)
_role_perms: dict[uuid.UUID, tuple[frozenset[str], float]] = {}
_lock = threading.Lock()


def _ttl() -> float:
    return settings.PERMISSIONS_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS


def _role_ids_for_user(session: Session, user_id: uuid.UUID) -> tuple[uuid.UUID, ...]:
    """Cached ``user -> role ids`` lookup (one small query per user)."""
    now = time.monotonic()
    with _lock:
        entry = _user_roles.get(user_id)
        if entry is not None and entry[1] > now:
            return entry[0]

    role_ids = tuple(
        session.exec(
            select(UserRole.role_id).where(col(UserRole.user_id) == user_id)
        ).all()
    )
    with _lock:
        _user_roles[user_id] = (role_ids, time.monotonic() + _ttl())
    return role_ids


def _permission_names_for_role(session: Session, role_id: uuid.UUID) -> frozenset[str]:
    """Cached ``role -> permission names`` lookup, shared across all users."""
    now = time.monotonic()
    with _lock:
        entry = _role_perms.get(role_id)
        if entry is not None and entry[1] > now:
            return entry[0]

    names = frozenset(
        session.exec(
            select(Permission.name)
            .select_from(RolePermission)
            .join(
                Permission,
                col(Permission.id) == col(RolePermission.permission_id),
            )
            .where(col(RolePermission.role_id) == role_id)
        ).all()
    )
    with _lock:
        _role_perms[role_id] = (names, time.monotonic() + _ttl())
    return names


def resolve_permissions(session: Session, user: User) -> set[str]:
    """Return the user's effective permission names, composed from both layers."""
    perms: set[str] = set()
    for role_id in _role_ids_for_user(session, user.id):
        perms |= _permission_names_for_role(session, role_id)
    return perms


def invalidate_user(user_id: uuid.UUID) -> None:
    """Drop one user's cached role ids (role assignment changed, deactivation...)."""
    with _lock:
        _user_roles.pop(user_id, None)


def invalidate_role(role_id: uuid.UUID) -> None:
    """Drop one role's cached permissions (its permission set changed).

    Every user holding the role sees the change on their next request, with a
    single re-read of this role -- no per-user invalidation needed.
    """
    with _lock:
        _role_perms.pop(role_id, None)


def invalidate_all() -> None:
    """Drop every cached entry (e.g. after re-seeding roles/permissions)."""
    with _lock:
        _user_roles.clear()
        _role_perms.clear()

content.text:
Done — the cache now works exactly as you described, and it's committed and pushed to PR #4.

## What's cached now (two layers)
```python
_user_roles: dict[user_id -> (tuple[role_id, ...], expiry)]      # per user, small
_role_perms: dict[role_id -> (frozenset[perm_name], expiry)]     # shared by all holders
```
`resolve_permissions` composes them in memory: look up the user's role ids (cached), union each role's permission names (cached). So:
- **`role → permissions`** — the expensive, rarely-changing join — is resolved **once per role** and reused by every user holding it, instead of re-walking the full `user→role→permission` join and caching a flattened copy per user. With few roles and many users, that's the big saving.
- **`user → roles`** is the only per-user entry, and it's tiny.
- **No `user → permission`** relation — all grants go through roles, as you said; nothing to support there.

## The gap question, resolved
- **Role *assignment* change** (admin edits a user's `role_ids`): no gap — `invalidate_user` already fires.
- **Role *definition* change** (a role's permission set changes): the new `invalidate_role(role_id)` drops that one shared entry, so **every holder** picks it up on their next request from a single re-read — no 60s wait, no global flush. (There's no endpoint that edits role permissions yet, but the hook is now in place for when one's added.)
- The 60s TTL is now purely a backstop for out-of-band DB edits or a multi-worker deploy.

## Verified & shipped
- Public API (`resolve_permissions` / `invalidate_user` / `invalidate_all`) and every call site unchanged.
- **80 tests pass** (added a test proving a role-permission change propagates to two holders via one `invalidate_role`, with no per-user invalidation), lint/type-check clean.
- Committed as `refactor(backend): cache user->roles and role->permissions in two layers` and pushed — **PR #4 now has 6 commits**. The live app is healthy on the new code.
